headline: Approved loan authorizations and transfers for 911 radio system, 7 Streets infrastructure project, Beaver Street rail crossing, and union pay raises.
summary: The committee approved a $1,000 donation to the Fire Department, a $1,675,000 loan authorization for a 911 dispatch radio system, and several fund transfers including $11,809.14 for survey equipment and $32,000 for the Beaver Street railroad crossing design. It also approved funding transfers of $678,550 for the Teamsters union contract and $1,158,400 for non-union compensation, plus financing for a $3,717,000 seven-street infrastructure project.
decisions: Approved accepting a $1,000 donation from the Revvity Foundation to the Waltham Fire Department.
Approved a first reading of a $1,675,000 loan authorization for a new Zetron Max station alerting and radio control system for the 911 Dispatch Center.
Approved a $11,809.14 transfer to purchase survey equipment for the Engineering Department.
Approved a transfer of $1,519,316 for the seven-street water/sewer/street infrastructure project.
Approved a first reading of a $2,125,684 loan authorization for the seven-street infrastructure project.
Approved a $32,000 transfer for additional design services for the Beaver Street railroad crossing project.
Approved a $678,550 funding transfer for the Teamsters (Laborers') Union collective bargaining agreement.
Approved a $1,158,400 funding transfer for the Non-Union Compensation Ordinance amendment.

plain_text:
FINANCE COMMITTEE 
Minutes of the Meeting  
August 3, 2026 
 
1.  Chairman Katz called the meeting to order at 11:20pm in the City Council Chamber. 
 
2.  Chairman Katz requested that a roll call be taken to record the attendance for the 
meeting.  The Clerk called the roll – Committee members Durkee, King, LaFauci, LeBlanc 
and Chairman Katz were all present in-person. 
 
3.  Councillor Durkee moved to accept the minutes of the meeting held on June 2 2, 2026.  
The motion was adopted on a voice vote and the minutes of the meeting on June 2 2, 
2026. 
 
4.  A motion to hear from individuals with an item on the docket (Fire Chief Mullin, City 
Engineer Winn, Traffic Engineer Garvin, and City Auditor Centofanti) was adopted on a 
voice vote. 
 
5.  A request was received from the Mayor to approve the acceptance of a donation from the 
Revvity Foundation in the amount of $1,000 to the Waltham Fire Department to support 
its organization and endeavors.  Chief Mullin provided a brief explanation of the 
proposed use of the gift funds.  A motion by Councillor LaFauci to accept the donation 
was adopted on a voice vote. 
 
6.  A request was received from the Mayor to approve the loan authorization in the amount of 
$1,675,000 for the purchase and installation of a new Zetron Max station alerting and 
radio control system for the 911 Dispatch Center.  Upon questions from Councillors, 
Chief Mullin gave a detailed explanation of the need and purpose of the radio system.  A 
notion by Councillor LaFauci to give the loan authorization a first reading was adopted on 
a voice vote. 
 
7.  A request was received from the Mayor to approve a transfer in the amount of $11,809.14 
to purchase survey equipment for the in-house survey work that is performed by the 
Engineering Department staff. 
 
FROM: 
Engineer – Parking Lot Improvements #001-410-5800-6320  $11,809.14 
TO: 
Engineer – Survey Equipment    #001-410-5800-6471  $11,809.14 
 
Upon questions from Councillors, Mr. Winn explained the need and the purpose for how 
the equipment would be used.  A motion by Councillor Durkee to approve the transfer 
was adopted on a voice vote.
8.  A request was received from the Mayor to approve a financing transaction in the total 
amount of $3,717,000 for a water/sewer/street infrastructure project for the following 
seven (7) streets – Bolton, Caughey, Clinton, Cutter, Day, Graymore and Mt. Pleasant.  
The total amount includes the bid amount ($3,548,878.51), construction administration 
($117,000), and a contingency ($51,121.49). 
 
The financing transaction request includes approval of the attached loan authorization in 
the amount of $2,125,684 and approval of the following transfers totaling $1,591,316. 
 
FROM: 
Eng (ST)  – Lexington Street    #310-410-2024-6720   $   125,848 
Eng (ST) – Clark/Ripley/Gale/Peirce #310-410-2024-6740   $   115,076 
Eng (W) – Clark/Ripley/Gale/Peirce #613-450-2024-7440   $     80,406 
Eng (W) – Winter/Lincoln     #613-450-2024-7480   $1,073,581 
Eng (S) – Winter/Lincoln     #603-440-2019-7340   $     88,673 
Eng (S) – Clark/Ripley/Gale/Peirce  #603-440-2024-7380   $   107,732 
 
TO: 
Eng – 7 Streets (Street)     #310-410-2024-6730     $   240,924  
Eng – 7 Streets (Water)     #613-450-2024-7430     $1,153,987 
Eng  - 7 Streets (Sewer)     #603-440-2019-7330     $     88,673 
Eng – 7 Streets (Sewer)     #603-440-2024-7330     $   107,732 
 
 
Loan Authorization                   $2,125,684 
 
TOTAL                       $3,717,000 
 
Upon questions from Councillors King, LeBlanc, and LaFauci, Mr. Winn explained the 
scope of the work and the benefit of the improvements to be made.  A motion by 
Councillor King to approve the transfer of $1,519,316 was adopted on a voice vote.  A 
notion by Councillor LaFauci to give the loan authorization of $2,125,684 a first reading 
was adopted on a voice vote. 
 
9.  A request was received from the Mayor to approve a transfer of funds in the amount of 
$32,000 for the additional design services that were not included in the original scope of 
work for the Beaver Street railroad crossing project. 
 
FROM: 
Traffic Impact – Pulte Homes    #259-480-2908-5205  $32,000 
TO: 
Traffic Impact – Beaver St RR Design  #259-480-2980-5205  $32,000
Mr. Garvin gave an overview of the project stating the need to address safety impacts for 
vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians.  Councillor King asked follow up questions about 
the specific design elements of the project.  VP LeBlanc asked follow up questions about 
the impact on the rail trail.  A motion by Councillor King to approve the transfer was 
adopted on a voice vote. 
 
10.  A request was received from the Mayor to approve a funding transfer totaling $678,550 
to fund the first year and the second year of the three-year collective bargaining 
agreement between the City and the Teamsters (Laborers’) Union for the period July 1, 
2025 to June 30, 2028.  The funding for the third year of the agreement will be 
recommended in the FY2028 operating budget for each applicable department.  
 
TRANSFER FROM: 
Auditor – Collective Bargaining  #001-135-5400-5111    $678,550 
TRANSFER TO: 
Various department wage accounts           $678,550 
  
In addition to the compensation, agreement was reached on several items that will 
mutually benefit both City Management and the Union.  Upon questions from Councillor 
King, Mr. Centofanti explained several elements of the agreement.  A motion by 
Councillor King to approve the transfer was adopted on a voice vote. 
  
11. A request was received from the Mayor to approve a funding transfer totaling $1,158,400 
to fund the first year and the second year of the three-year amendment to the Non-
Union Compensation Ordinance covering the period July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2028.  The 
funding for the third year of the proposed ordinance amendment will be recommended in 
the FY2028 operating budget for each applicable department.   
 
TRANSFER FROM: 
Auditor – Collective Bargaining  #001-135-5400-5111    $1,158,400 
TRANSFER TO: 
Various department salary accounts           $1,158,400 
 
Due to a conflict, Councillor King recused himself from the discussion and vote on the 
matter.  Upon questions from Councillor Durkee, Mr. Centofanti explained the 
compensation increase was consistent with the agreement reached with the other unions.  
A motion by Councillor Durkee to approve the transfer was adopted on a voice vote. 
 
      
12. A motion by Councillor Durkee to adjourn was adopted on a voice vote and Chairman 
Katz declared the meeting adjourned at 11:45pm. 
 
 
Paul G. Centofanti – Clerk to the Finance Committee
